character: 4.563km, 16 turns, clockwise at the foot of Mount Fuji. A 1.475km main straight — one of the longest anywhere — feeds the hardest braking zone on the lap, then a fast downhill middle sector, then a tight technical final third. Exit speed from the last corner sets top speed down the entire straight, so the lap is won at the end of it.
sources: official Fuji Speedway circuit guide (FIA WEC 6H of Fuji programme, https://storage.googleapis.com/fiawec-prod/assets/fileuploads/5d/8a/5d8a3c3a63038.pdf) for the sponsor-named sections (TGR, Coca-Cola, Toyopet 100R, Advan, 300R, Dunlop, GR Supra, Panasonic) and their character; https://www.racingcircuits.info/asia/japan/fuji-speedway.html for the 4.563 km / 16-turn layout.
notes: Entries are deliberately unanchored: bundled registry facts for Fuji are auto-seeded from AC Evo's racing line and hold 9 unnamed regions, so T1..T9 are not circuit's official 1..16 and there is nothing honest to anchor to. Registered in test/track-guide-anchor.test.ts.

corners.name: TGR Corner
corners.type: sharp right-hander at the end of the 1.475km straight (Turn 1)
corners.technique: Brake as late as you dare from top speed, straight-line the braking, late apex to open the exit
corners.trap: Braking judgement from that approach speed is the whole corner — early braking throws away the straight, late braking locks the inside front

corners.name: Coca-Cola Corner
corners.technique: Patience — the corner keeps tightening, so hold something in reserve and wait for it to open before full throttle
corners.trap: Committing to an early apex, then having to lift as the radius closes

corners.name: Toyopet 100R
corners.technique: Carry speed in on one line — there is effectively only one line through here — and let the car run wide on exit
corners.trap: Scrubbing the front by asking for more angle mid-corner instead of settling on the entry line

corners.name: Advan Corner
corners.type: tight left hairpin, the slowest point on the circuit (~60-70 km/h)
corners.technique: Heavy braking down from 100R, late apex, patient throttle — the exit runs slightly uphill into 300R
corners.trap: Over-slowing or spinning the rears on exit costs all the way through 300R

corners.name: 300R
corners.technique: Near-flat with a light lift, minimal steering input — this is a momentum corner feeding the downhill run
corners.trap: Any correction here bleeds the speed you need for the Dunlop braking zone

corners.name: Dunlop Corner
corners.type: downhill braking zone where lines cross — the circuit's other big overtaking spot
corners.technique: Brake precisely on the downhill, expect the car to be light on the way in, commit to one line early
corners.trap: Braking downhill with the car unloaded locks fronts; drifting off line invites a switchback

corners.name: GR Supra Corner
corners.technique: Careful throttle application — line choice genuinely varies by car and driver here, so settle on one and repeat it
corners.trap: Chasing a different line every lap; inconsistency through sector 3 costs more than the corner itself

corners.name: Panasonic Corner
corners.type: uphill final right onto the main straight (Turn 16)
corners.technique: Prioritise exit over entry: sacrifice apex speed for a clean, early-throttle exit — this corner sets your top speed for 1.475km
corners.trap: A tidy-looking fast entry that compromises exit is the single most expensive mistake on the lap
